For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	"""Offline light-client verification of externally supplied proof bundles.
2	
3	A proof bundle lets a client verify ledger responses without trusting the
4	serving node or holding any chain state:
5	
6	    bundle = {
7	        "source": str,
8	        "expires_at": int,            # Unix seconds
9	        "response": object,           # the attested response object
10	        "candidate": [...],           # full block list starting at genesis
11	        "proofs": [                   # optional Merkle inclusion proofs
12	            {"height": int, "proof": {height, tx_id, index, merkle_root,
13	                                      block_hash, siblings}},
14	            ...
15	        ],
16	        # Optional account-state extension: all four fields are either present
17	        # together or absent together, and state_proofs is a non-empty list.
18	        "state_root": str,            # 64 lowercase hex, anchored state root
19	        "state_height": int,          # confirmed anchor block height
20	        "state_block_hash": str,      # 64 lowercase hex anchor block hash
21	        "state_proofs": [             # account-state inclusion proofs
22	            {"height": int, "proof": {account, balance,
23	                                      confirmed_transactions, index,
24	                                      state_root, height, block_hash,
25	                                      siblings}},
26	            ...
27	        ],
28	        "signature": str,             # optional Ed25519 signature hex
29	    }
30	
31	The local trust document pins the genesis block hash and records, per source,
32	an optional Ed25519 public key with its own expiry, plus an allowlist of
33	sources accepted without signatures:
34	
35	    trust = {
36	        "genesis_hash": "<64 lowercase hex chars>",
37	        "sources": {source: {"public_key": hex, "expires_at": int}},
38	        "allowlist": {source: expires_at_int},
39	    }
40	
41	Verification, in order:
42	
43	1. **input** — bundle and trust must have the documented shape; every numeric
44	   field must be a plain (non-boolean) integer.
45	2. **auth** — the source must be trusted (a ``sources`` entry or the
46	   ``allowlist``). A source with a public key must sign the bundle; a bundle
47	   carrying a signature for a key-less source, or an unsigned bundle from a
48	   non-allowlisted source, fails.
49	3. **expired** — neither the bundle deadline nor the trust entry's deadline
50	   may have passed (``expires_at <= now`` counts as expired).
51	4. **integrity** — the signature (when required) is verified over
52	   Ed25519(sha256(sorted-compact UTF-8 JSON of the bundle without
53	   ``signature``)); the candidate chain is recomputed from the pinned genesis
54	   (heights, prev_hash linkage, every transaction's tx_id and Ed25519
55	   signature, unique tx_ids, Merkle roots, block hashes, pending-only-at-tip)
56	   and the response's descriptor fields are checked against the recomputed
57	   tip descriptor ``S``.
58	5. **proof** — every proof must be unique, its tx_id/height/index and block
59	   fields must agree with the candidate block, the Merkle path must verify
60	   under the existing rules, and its block must not be the pending tip. When
61	   the state extension is present, its anchor (``state_height`` /
62	   ``state_block_hash``) must name a confirmed candidate block (integrity) and
63	   every state proof must agree with both anchor heights, the state root and
64	   the anchor hash; each account must sit at its ``index`` in the ascending
65	   account set of the anchor height's confirmed transactions, ``height`` +
66	   ``account`` pairs must be unique, and every proof must pass
67	   ``crypto.verify_account_proof`` against the bundle's anchors.
68	
69	On success :func:`verify_bundle` returns
70	``{"ok": True, "source", "S", "verified_tx_ids"}`` — plus
71	``"verified_accounts"`` (ascending) when the state extension was verified —
72	on failure ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
73	``input/auth/expired/integrity/proof``.
74	
75	:func:`verify_range_export` verifies one exported incremental range delivery
76	(the ``GET /v1/forks/sync/range/export`` document, top-level key order
77	``source, request_id, mode, expires_at, anchor, blocks, tip, attestation``)
78	offline against a caller-pinned expected anchor and the local trust document.
79	The expected anchor must strictly equal the document's ``anchor``; the
80	delivered tail is recomputed standalone from that anchor (consecutive
81	heights, prev_hash linkage, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signatures,
82	unique and block-ascending tx_ids, Merkle roots, block hashes,
83	pending-only-at-tip) and the closed ``tip`` summary must recompute. A
84	``plain`` export must come from an unexpired ``allowlist`` entry and carry
85	``attestation: null``. An ``attested`` export is authenticated by key
86	version: when the trust document carries a ``source_key_history`` mapping,
87	the attestation's ``version`` selects that source's historical public key
88	(which must equal the attestation's ``public_key``); an unknown source or
89	version, or a mismatched key, is ``auth`` and a signature that fails to
90	verify is ``integrity`` — so an export signed under a since-rotated key
91	stays verifiable. A trust document without ``source_key_history`` keeps the
92	legacy rule: the source must be an unexpired ``trust.sources`` entry whose
93	pinned key matches the attestation and verifies the Ed25519 signature over
94	the SHA-256 digest of the canonical ``ledger-sync-range-v1`` message.
95	Failures map to ``input`` (structure), ``auth`` (authorization), ``expired``
96	(deadlines) and ``integrity`` (anchor/chain/signature); nothing is raised.
97	Success returns ``{"ok": True, "source", "request_id", "mode", "anchor",
98	"tip", "verified_tx_ids"}`` with ``verified_tx_ids`` ascending.
99	
100	:func:`verify_range_exports` verifies an ordered, non-empty batch of such
101	range deliveries as one continuous chain. The first page's anchor must equal
102	the caller-pinned ``expected_anchor``; every later page's anchor must equal
103	the previous page's closed tip's ``{height, block_hash}``. Each page is
104	re-verified under the same input/auth/expired/integrity rules, transaction
105	ids are unique across the whole batch, and a pending block may only appear on
106	the last page — a broken anchor, a height jump, a duplicate transaction or any
107	block after a pending one is an ``integrity`` failure. Success returns
108	``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "pages", "verified_tx_ids"}`` with ``tip``
109	the last page's tip, ``pages`` the page count and ``verified_tx_ids``
110	ascending; failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one
111	of ``input/auth/expired/integrity``.
112	"""
113	from __future__ import annotations

124	# Stable error categories returned to callers.
125	ERR_INPUT = "input"
126	ERR_AUTH = "auth"
127	ERR_EXPIRED = "expired"
128	ERR_INTEGRITY = "integrity"
129	ERR_PROOF = "proof"

131	# Descriptor fields of a chain tip, exactly as GET /v1/chain reports them.
132	DESCRIPTOR_FIELDS = ("tip_hash", "height", "length", "status")
133	
134	# The optional account-state extension: these four bundle fields are either
135	# all present or all absent.
136	STATE_FIELDS = ("state_root", "state_height", "state_block_hash", "state_proofs")

138	# The exact key set of one state-proof document (mirrors the server's
139	# GET /v1/accounts/{account}/proof response).
140	_STATE_PROOF_KEYS = frozenset(
141	    (
142	        "account",
143	        "balance",
144	        "confirmed_transactions",
145	        "index",
146	        "state_root",
147	        "height",
148	        "block_hash",
149	        "siblings",

153	# An Ed25519 public key rendered as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
154	_HEX32_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}")

156	
157	class _Failure(Exception):
158	    """Internal control-flow exception carrying the public error category."""
159	
160	    def __init__(self, category: str) -> None:
161	        self.category = category
162	        super().__init__(category)
163	
164	
165	def _is_int(value: object) -> bool:
166	    """Plain integer test; booleans are rejected (bool subclasses int)."""
167	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
168	
169	
170	def canonical_bundle_bytes(bundle: dict) -> bytes:
171	    """Sorted, compact UTF-8 JSON of the bundle with its signature removed.
172	
173	    This is the exact byte document whose SHA-256 the source signs, so signers
174	    and verifiers always agree regardless of incoming key order. The
175	    serialization mirrors :func:`ledger.crypto.canonical_message`: sorted keys,
176	    compact separators, UTF-8 bytes.
177	    """
178	    unsigned = {key: value for key, value in bundle.items() if key != "signature"}
179	    return json.dumps(
180	        unsigned, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
181	    ).encode("utf-8")
182	
183	
184	def bundle_signing_digest(bundle: dict) -> bytes:
185	    """The 32-byte SHA-256 digest covered by a bundle Ed25519 signature."""
186	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical_bundle_bytes(bundle)).digest()
187	
188	
189	def verify_bundle(bundle: object, trust: object, now: float | None = None) -> dict:
190	    """Verify an offline proof bundle against the local trust document.
191	
192	    Returns ``{"ok": True, "source": ..., "S": ..., "verified_tx_ids": [...]}``
193	    on success — extended bundles also carry ``"verified_accounts"`` — or
194	    ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` on failure. Never raises for
195	    malformed input: every defect maps to one of the five categories.
196	    """
197	    current = time.time() if now is None else now
198	    try:
199	        source, candidate = _validate_inputs(bundle, trust)
200	        _authenticate(bundle, trust, source, current)
201	        blocks_raw = candidate["blocks"] if isinstance(candidate, dict) else candidate
202	        blocks = _recompute_chain(blocks_raw, trust)
203	        descriptor = _tip_descriptor(blocks)
204	        _check_candidate_summary(candidate, descriptor)
205	        _check_response(bundle["response"], descriptor)
206	        has_state = "state_root" in bundle
207	        if has_state:
208	            _check_state_anchor(bundle, blocks)
209	        verified_ids = _verify_proofs(bundle["proofs"], blocks)
210	        verified_accounts = (
211	            _verify_state_proofs(bundle, blocks) if has_state else None
212	        )
213	    except _Failure as failure:
214	        return {"ok": False, "error": failure.category}
215	    except Exception:
216	        # Defensive: structurally unforeseeable inputs must report rather than
217	        # crash the verifying process.
218	        return {"ok": False, "error": ERR_INPUT}
219	    result = {
220	        "ok": True,
221	        "source": source,
222	        "S": descriptor,
223	        "verified_tx_ids": verified_ids,
224	    }
225	    if verified_accounts is not None:
226	        result["verified_accounts"] = verified_accounts
227	    return result
228

230	# -- stage 1: shape -----------------------------------------------------------
231	
232	
233	def _validate_inputs(bundle: object, trust: object) -> tuple[str, object]:
234	    """Structural validation of bundle and trust.
235	
236	    Returns ``(source, candidate)`` where ``candidate`` is the raw candidate
237	    value (a bare block list or an export-format object carrying ``blocks``).
238	    The bundle itself is never mutated: the signature covers it verbatim.
239	    """
240	    if not isinstance(bundle, dict):
241	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
242	    for field in ("source", "expires_at", "response", "candidate", "proofs"):
243	        if field not in bundle:
244	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
245	    source = bundle["source"]
246	    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
247	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
248	    if not _is_int(bundle["expires_at"]):
249	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
250	    # The response is itself a JSON object; anything else cannot be checked
251	    # against the recomputed chain descriptor.
252	    if not isinstance(bundle["response"], dict):
253	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
254	    candidate = bundle["candidate"]
255	    blocks_raw = candidate.get("blocks") if isinstance(candidate, dict) else candidate
256	    if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list) or not blocks_raw:
257	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
258	    if not isinstance(bundle["proofs"], list):
259	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
260	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
261	    if signature is not None and (not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature):
262	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
263	    _validate_state_fields(bundle)
264	
265	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
266	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
267	    if not crypto.is_hex64(trust.get("genesis_hash")):
268	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
269	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
270	    if not isinstance(sources, dict):
271	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
272	    for name, entry in sources.items():
273	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not isinstance(entry, dict):
274	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
275	        if not _is_int(entry.get("expires_at")):
276	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
277	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
278	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
279	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
280	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
281	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
282	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
283	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
284	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
285	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
286	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
287	    return source, candidate
288	
289	
290	def _validate_state_fields(bundle: dict) -> None:
291	    """Structural validation of the optional account-state extension.
292	
293	    The four state fields are all-or-nothing; when present, ``state_root`` and
294	    ``state_block_hash`` must be 64-char lowercase hex, ``state_height`` a
295	    non-boolean non-negative integer and ``state_proofs`` a non-empty list.
296	    Every item must carry exactly ``{height, proof}`` and every proof document
297	    exactly the eight documented keys with the right JSON types. Only shape
298	    and type are judged here — domain defects (bad hex, negative balances,
299	    illegal directions) are reported later as integrity/proof failures.
300	    """
301	    present = [field for field in STATE_FIELDS if field in bundle]
302	    if not present:
303	        return
304	    if len(present) != len(STATE_FIELDS):
305	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
306	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_root"]):
307	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
308	    if not _is_int(bundle["state_height"]) or bundle["state_height"] < 0:
309	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
310	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_block_hash"]):
311	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
312	    state_proofs = bundle["state_proofs"]
313	    if not isinstance(state_proofs, list) or not state_proofs:
314	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
315	    for item in state_proofs:
316	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != {"height", "proof"}:
317	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
318	        if not _is_int(item["height"]):
319	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
320	        proof = item["proof"]
321	        if not isinstance(proof, dict) or set(proof) != _STATE_PROOF_KEYS:
322	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
323	        if not isinstance(proof["account"], str) or not proof["account"]:
324	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
325	        if not _is_int(proof["balance"]):
326	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
327	        transactions = proof["confirmed_transactions"]
328	        if not isinstance(transactions, list) or any(
329	            not isinstance(tx_id, str) for tx_id in transactions
330	        ):
331	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
332	        if not _is_int(proof["index"]):
333	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
334	        if not isinstance(proof["state_root"], str):
335	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
336	        if not _is_int(proof["height"]):
337	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
338	        if not isinstance(proof["block_hash"], str):
339	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
340	        if not isinstance(proof["siblings"], list):
341	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
342

344	# -- stage 2/3: trust, expiry and signature -----------------------------------
345	
346	
347	def _authenticate(
348	    bundle: dict, trust: dict, source: str, now: float
349	) -> None:
350	    """Check source trust, every deadline and the optional Ed25519 signature."""
351	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
352	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
353	    source_entry = sources.get(source)
354	    allowlist_expiry = allowlist.get(source)
355	    if source_entry is None and allowlist_expiry is None:
356	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
357	
358	    # All deadlines are checked before any signature work: an expired,
359	    # correctly-signed bundle is still unusable. A source listed in both
360	    # ``sources`` and ``allowlist`` is bound by both deadlines.
361	    if bundle["expires_at"] <= now:
362	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
363	    if source_entry is not None and source_entry["expires_at"] <= now:
364	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
365	    if allowlist_expiry is not None and allowlist_expiry <= now:
366	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
367	
368	    public_key = source_entry.get("public_key") if source_entry else None
369	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
370	    if public_key is not None:
371	        # A keyed source must sign: a missing signature cannot authenticate.
372	        if signature is None:
373	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
374	        if not crypto.verify_signature(
375	            public_key, bundle_signing_digest(bundle), signature
376	        ):
377	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
378	        return
379	    # The source reached this point only through the allowlist (every sources
380	    # entry pins a key). An unsigned allowlisted bundle is therefore accepted;
381	    # a signature with no pinned key to check it against is meaningless.
382	    if signature is not None:
383	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
384

386	# -- stage 4: chain recomputation and response cross-check --------------------
387	
388	
389	def _tip_descriptor(blocks: list[Block]) -> dict:
390	    tip = blocks[-1]
391	    return {
392	        "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
393	        "height": tip.height,
394	        "length": len(blocks),
395	        "status": tip.status,
396	    }
397	
398	
399	def _recompute_chain(candidate_raw: list, trust: dict) -> list[Block]:
400	    """Recompute and validate the whole candidate chain from the pinned genesis.
401	
402	    Mirrors the node's own candidate rules except the endowment balance replay
403	    (an offline client holds no balance convention): genesis anchor, heights,
404	    prev_hash linkage, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signatures, unique
405	    tx_id-sorted transactions, Merkle roots, block hashes and the
406	    pending-only-at-tip rule. Every field is checked on the *raw* JSON value so
407	    coercions such as ``"1"`` or ``1.0`` heights are rejected outright; such
408	    type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height, non-positive or
409	    non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while recomputation
410	    mismatches stay ``integrity``.
411	    """
412	    blocks: list[Block] = []
413	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
414	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(candidate_raw):
415	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
416	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
417	        height = block_raw.get("height")
418	        prev_hash = block_raw.get("prev_hash")
419	        merkle_root = block_raw.get("merkle_root")
420	        block_hash = block_raw.get("block_hash")
421	        status = block_raw.get("status")
422	        txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
423	        # A height of the wrong type or sign is a field-type defect (input),
424	        # not a chain mismatch: strings, floats and booleans must never be
425	        # coerced into plausible integers before the linkage checks below.
426	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
427	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
428	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
429	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
430	        if not crypto.is_hex64(merkle_root) or not crypto.is_hex64(block_hash):
431	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
432	        if status not in ("pending", "confirmed") or not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
433	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
434	        if height != position:
435	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
436	        expected_prev = (
437	            GENESIS_PREV_HASH if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
438	        )
439	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
440	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
441	        if position == 0:
442	            # Genesis must be the exact block the client pinned: confirmed,
443	            # empty, and carrying the trusted hash (recomputed below too).
444	            if status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or txs_raw:
445	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
446	            if block_hash != trust["genesis_hash"]:
447	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
448	        elif position < len(candidate_raw) - 1 and status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
449	            # A pending block may only sit at the chain tip.
450	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
451	
452	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
453	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
454	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):
455	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
456	            sender = raw_tx.get("from")
457	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
458	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
459	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
460	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")
461	            if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
462	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
463	            if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
464	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
465	            # Same rule as the block height: the raw amount must already be a
466	            # non-boolean positive integer — never a coercible string, float
467	            # or bool — so a domain/type defect is reported as input.
468	            if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
469	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
470	            if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
471	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
472	            message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
473	            tx_id = crypto.compute_tx_id(message)
474	            if stored_tx_id != tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
475	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
476	            if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
477	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
478	            if tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
479	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
480	            seen_tx_ids.add(tx_id)
481	            tx_ids.append(tx_id)
482	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
483	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
484	        if crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids) != merkle_root:
485	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
486	        recomputed = compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle_root)
487	        if recomputed != block_hash:
488	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
489	        # Parsed only after every raw field has checked out; never trusted for
490	        # the comparison decisions above.
491	        try:
492	            blocks.append(Block.from_dict(block_raw))
493	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
494	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
495	    return blocks
496

498	def _check_candidate_summary(candidate: object, descriptor: dict) -> None:
499	    """Cross-check an export-format candidate's own tip summary fields.
500	
501	    A bare block list has nothing to check. A five-field export document's
502	    supplied ``tip_hash/height/length/status`` must equal the recomputed tip
503	    descriptor, exactly as the node requires on resubmission.
504	    """
505	    if not isinstance(candidate, dict):
506	        return
507	    for field in DESCRIPTOR_FIELDS:
508	        if field in candidate and candidate[field] != descriptor[field]:
509	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
510	
511	
512	def _check_response(response: dict, descriptor: dict) -> None:
513	    """Every descriptor field present in the response must equal the tip's.
514	
515	    A response carrying none of the descriptor fields cannot be bound to the
516	    recomputed chain at all, so it is rejected rather than vacuously accepted.
517	    """
518	    matched = False
519	    for field in DESCRIPTOR_FIELDS:
520	        if field in response:
521	            matched = True
522	            if response[field] != descriptor[field]:
523	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
524	    if not matched:
525	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
526	
527	
528	def _check_state_anchor(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> None:
529	    """Bind the state extension's anchor to the recomputed candidate chain.
530	
531	    ``state_height`` must name a confirmed candidate block whose hash equals
532	    ``state_block_hash``; an unknown height, a pending block or a hash
533	    mismatch is an integrity failure. Every state-proof item and document
534	    must agree with both anchor heights, the bundle's state root and the
535	    anchor block hash.
536	    """
537	    height = bundle["state_height"]
538	    state_root = bundle["state_root"]
539	    block_hash = bundle["state_block_hash"]
540	    if height >= len(blocks):
541	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
542	    block = blocks[height]
543	    if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or block.block_hash != block_hash:
544	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
545	    for item in bundle["state_proofs"]:
546	        proof = item["proof"]
547	        if item["height"] != height or proof["height"] != height:
548	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
549	        if proof["state_root"] != state_root or proof["block_hash"] != block_hash:
550	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
551

553	# -- stage 5: proofs ----------------------------------------------------------
554	
555	
556	def _verify_proofs(proofs_raw: list, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
557	    """Validate uniqueness and cross-block consistency of every proof.
558	
559	    Each entry is ``{"height": int, "proof": doc}`` and the proof document
560	    follows the server shape ``{height, tx_id, index, merkle_root, block_hash,
561	    siblings}``. Proofs for the pending tip are forbidden. The verified
562	    transaction ids are returned sorted ascending.
563	    """
564	    verified: list[str] = []
565	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
566	    for item in proofs_raw:
567	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
568	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
569	        height = item.get("height")
570	        proof = item.get("proof")
571	        if not _is_int(height) or not isinstance(proof, dict):
572	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
573	        if height < 0 or height >= len(blocks):
574	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
575	        block = blocks[height]
576	        if block.height != height:
577	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
578	        # Pending tips never carry trustworthy proofs.
579	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
580	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
581	
582	        tx_id = proof.get("tx_id")
583	        index = proof.get("index")
584	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id) or not _is_int(index):
585	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
586	        # The item height and the proof document's own fields must agree with
587	        # the candidate block they claim inclusion in.
588	        if proof.get("height") != height or proof.get("block_hash") != block.block_hash:
589	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
590	        if proof.get("merkle_root") != block.merkle_root:
591	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
592	        if index < 0 or index >= len(block.transactions):
593	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
594	        if block.transactions[index].tx_id != tx_id:
595	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
596	
597	        key = (height, tx_id)
598	        if key in seen:
599	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
600	        seen.add(key)
601	
602	        if not crypto.verify_merkle_proof(
603	            tx_id,
604	            proof.get("siblings"),
605	            block.merkle_root,
606	            block.block_hash,
607	            block.block_hash,
608	        ):
609	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
610	        verified.append(tx_id)

614	def _verify_state_proofs(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
615	    """Verify every account-state proof against the bundle's state anchor.
616	
617	    The anchor's confirmed transactions determine the ascending account set;
618	    each proof's ``account`` must belong to it and its ``index`` must be the
619	    account's position in that ordering. ``height`` + ``account`` pairs must
620	    be unique. Every proof is then checked with
621	    :func:`crypto.verify_account_proof` against the bundle's ``state_root``,
622	    ``state_height`` and ``state_block_hash``; any failure — an illegal
623	    direction or hash, a forged leaf, an illegal self-pair, a malformed
624	    sibling path — is a proof failure. Returns the verified accounts sorted
625	    ascending.
626	    """
627	    height = bundle["state_height"]
628	    # The account set of the anchor height: every account touched by a
629	    # confirmed transaction up to and including the anchor block, ascending.
630	    accounts: set[str] = set()
631	    for block in blocks[: height + 1]:
632	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
633	            continue
634	        for tx in block.transactions:
635	            accounts.add(tx.sender)
636	            accounts.add(tx.recipient)
637	    position = {account: index for index, account in enumerate(sorted(accounts))}
638	
639	    verified: list[str] = []
640	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
641	    for item in bundle["state_proofs"]:
642	        proof = item["proof"]
643	        account = proof["account"]
644	        expected = position.get(account)
645	        # An account outside the anchor's set, or an index that is not the
646	        # account's ascending position (including out-of-range), is a proof
647	        # failure.
648	        if expected is None or proof["index"] != expected:
649	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
650	        key = (item["height"], account)
651	        if key in seen:
652	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
653	        seen.add(key)
654	        if not crypto.verify_account_proof(
655	            proof,
656	            bundle["state_root"],
657	            height,
658	            bundle["state_block_hash"],
659	        ):
660	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
661	        verified.append(account)
662	    return sorted(verified)

744	def verify_range_exports(
745	    documents: object,
746	    expected_anchor: object,
747	    trust: object,
748	    now: int | float | None = None,
749	) -> dict:
750	    """Verify an ordered batch of exported range deliveries as one chain.
751	
752	    ``documents`` must be a non-empty list of decoded
753	    ``GET /v1/forks/sync/range/export`` documents (each with the exact key
754	    order ``source, request_id, mode, expires_at, anchor, blocks, tip,
755	    attestation``); ``expected_anchor`` is the caller-pinned
756	    ``{height, block_hash}`` the first page's anchor must strictly equal;
757	    ``trust`` is the local trust document applied to every page.
758	
759	    The pages are re-verified in order: the first page is checked against
760	    ``expected_anchor``, and every later page's anchor must strictly equal the
761	    previous page's closed ``tip`` reduced to ``{height, block_hash}`` — which
762	    also rejects a height jump or a fork at the seam. Transaction ids must be
763	    unique across the whole batch, not just inside one page, and a pending
764	    block may only appear on the last page.
765	
766	    Returns ``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "pages", "verified_tx_ids"}`` on
767	    success — ``anchor`` the pinned anchor of the first page, ``tip`` the last
768	    page's closed tip, ``pages`` the number of pages and
769	    ``verified_tx_ids`` ascending across every page — or
770	    ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` on failure with category one of
771	    ``input/auth/expired/integrity``. Never raises for malformed input.
772	    """
773	    current = time.time() if now is None else now
774	    try:
775	        if not isinstance(documents, list) or not documents:
776	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
777	        # The pinned anchor is validated once up front so a malformed caller
778	        # anchor is an input error even before the first page is inspected.
779	        anchor = _validate_range_anchor(expected_anchor)
780	        _validate_range_trust(trust)
781	        pages = len(documents)
782	        expected = anchor
783	        first_anchor: dict | None = None
784	        last_tip: dict | None = None
785	        seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
786	        verified_ids: list[str] = []
787	        for position, document in enumerate(documents):
788	            # _verify_range_page itself rejects a page whose anchor does not
789	            # strictly equal ``expected`` — the first page's pinned anchor and
790	            # every later page's previous tip — so a broken seam or a height
791	            # jump surfaces as integrity here.
792	            page_anchor, tip, page_tx_ids = _verify_range_page(
793	                document, expected, trust, current
794	            )
795	            if first_anchor is None:
796	                first_anchor = page_anchor
797	            # Transaction ids must be unique across pages, not merely within
798	            # one re-verified tail.
799	            duplicates = seen_tx_ids.intersection(page_tx_ids)
800	            if duplicates:
801	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
802	            seen_tx_ids.update(page_tx_ids)
803	            verified_ids.extend(page_tx_ids)
804	            # A pending block may only sit on the very last page: any block
805	            # delivered after a pending tip breaks the continuous confirmed
806	            # chain and cannot be linked to a committed predecessor.
807	            if tip["status"] == STATUS_PENDING and position != pages - 1:
808	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
809	            last_tip = tip
810	            expected = {"height": tip["height"], "block_hash": tip["tip_hash"]}
811	    except _Failure as failure:
812	        return {"ok": False, "error": failure.category}
813	    except Exception:
814	        # Defensive: structurally unforeseeable inputs must report rather than
815	        # crash the verifying process.
816	        return {"ok": False, "error": ERR_INPUT}
817	    return {
818	        "ok": True,
819	        "anchor": first_anchor,
820	        "tip": last_tip,
821	        "pages": pages,
822	        "verified_tx_ids": sorted(verified_ids),
823	    }

826	def _verify_range_page(
827	    document: object, expected_anchor: object, trust: object, now: float
828	) -> tuple[dict, dict, list[str]]:
829	    """Verify one range page, returning ``(anchor, tip, verified_tx_ids)``.
830	
831	    Shared core of :func:`verify_range_export` (one page) and
832	    :func:`verify_range_exports` (a batch chaining each page's tip into the
833	    next page's expected anchor). Raises :class:`_Failure` with the public
834	    error category on every defect.
835	    """
836	    anchor = _validate_range_export_inputs(document, expected_anchor, trust)
837	    _authenticate_range_export(document, trust, now)
838	    # The caller-pinned anchor must strictly equal the delivered one.
839	    if document["anchor"] != expected_anchor:
840	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
841	    tail = _recompute_range_tail(anchor, document["blocks"])
842	    tip = _range_tip_descriptor(anchor, tail)
843	    _check_range_tip(document["tip"], tip)
844	    if document["mode"] == "attested":
845	        _verify_range_attestation(document, trust)
846	    verified_ids = sorted(tx.tx_id for block in tail for tx in block.transactions)
847	    return anchor, tip, verified_ids

850	def _validate_range_export_inputs(
851	    document: object, expected_anchor: object, trust: object
852	) -> dict:
853	    """Structural validation of the export document, the pinned anchor and
854	    the trust document. Returns the closed ``{height, block_hash}`` anchor.
855	    """
856	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
857	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
858	    if tuple(document.keys()) != RANGE_EXPORT_KEYS:
859	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
860	    source = document["source"]
861	    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
862	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
863	    request_id = document["request_id"]
864	    if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
865	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
866	    if document["mode"] not in RANGE_EXPORT_MODES:
867	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
868	    if not _is_int(document["expires_at"]):
869	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
870	    anchor = _validate_range_anchor(document["anchor"])
871	    # The expected anchor is validated for shape here; the strict equality
872	    # binding itself is an integrity check after authorization and expiry.
873	    _validate_range_anchor(expected_anchor)
874	    blocks = document["blocks"]
875	    if not isinstance(blocks, list) or not blocks:
876	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
877	    tip = document["tip"]
878	    if not isinstance(tip, dict) or set(tip) != _RANGE_TIP_KEYS:
879	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
880	    if document["mode"] == "attested":
881	        attestation = document["attestation"]
882	        if not isinstance(attestation, dict) or set(attestation) != (
883	            _RANGE_ATTESTATION_KEYS
884	        ):
885	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
886	        if not crypto.is_hex64(attestation["public_key"]):
887	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

890	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
891	        if not crypto.is_hex128(attestation["signature"]):
892	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

909	def _validate_range_trust(trust: object) -> None:
910	    """Structural validation of the trust document's ``sources``/``allowlist``.
911	
912	    Mirrors the bundle verifier's trust rules; a ``genesis_hash`` is not
913	    required here because the caller pins the range anchor directly. The
914	    optional GET /v1/trust ``source_key_history`` mapping is validated too:
915	    each source maps to a non-empty ascending array of
916	    ``{version, public_key, activated_event_id}`` items whose versions are
917	    dense from 1 with strictly ascending activation ids, both numeric fields
918	    non-boolean positive integers and the public key 64 lowercase hex.
919	    """
920	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
921	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
922	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
923	    if not isinstance(sources, dict):
924	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
925	    for name, entry in sources.items():
926	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not isinstance(entry, dict):
927	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
928	        if not _is_int(entry.get("expires_at")):
929	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
930	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
931	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
932	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
933	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
934	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
935	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
936	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
937	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
938	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
939	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
940	    history = trust.get("source_key_history")
941	    if history is not None:
942	        if not isinstance(history, dict):
943	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
944	        for name, entries in history.items():
945	            if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
946	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
947	            if not isinstance(entries, list) or not entries:
948	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
949	            last_activated = None
950	            for position, entry in enumerate(entries):
951	                if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != set(
952	                    _HISTORY_ENTRY_KEYS
953	                ):
954	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
955	                version = entry.get("version")
956	                public_key = entry.get("public_key")
957	                activated = entry.get("activated_event_id")
958	                # Versions are dense from 1; both numeric fields are plain
959	                # (non-boolean) positive integers.
960	                if not _is_int(version) or version != position + 1:
961	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
962	                if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
963	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
964	                if not _is_int(activated) or activated < 1:
965	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
966	                if last_activated is not None and activated <= last_activated:
967	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
968	                last_activated = activated

976	def _authenticate_range_export(document: dict, trust: dict, now: float) -> None:
977	    """Check mode-specific source authorization and every deadline.
978	
979	    A ``plain`` export is only acceptable from an allowlisted source and must
980	    carry ``attestation: null``. An ``attested`` export is authorized one of
981	    two ways:
982	
983	    * the trust document carries a ``source_key_history`` mapping (the new
984	      rule): the source must appear in the mapping — the historical public key
985	      matching and signature verification happen by attestation version in
986	      :func:`_verify_range_attestation`; the trust ``sources`` entry and its
987	      deadline play no role, so a delivery signed under a since-rotated or
988	      revoked key still authenticates as long as the document itself is
989	      unexpired;
990	    * the mapping is absent (the legacy rule): the source must be a
991	      ``sources`` entry whose unexpired deadline is checked.
992	
993	    All deadlines are checked before any integrity work: an expired,
994	    correctly-signed export is still unusable.
995	    """
996	    source = document["source"]
997	    mode = document["mode"]
998	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
999	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
1000	    if mode == "plain":
1001	        if source not in allowlist:
1002	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1003	        # A plain export carrying an attestation is not a plain delivery.
1004	        if document["attestation"] is not None:
1005	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1006	    elif _has_key_history(trust):
1007	        # Historical-key authorization: the source (and later the attestation
1008	        # version) must resolve in the mapping; the current registry entry is
1009	        # deliberately not consulted.
1010	        if source not in trust["source_key_history"]:
1011	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1012	    elif source not in sources:
1013	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1014	
1015	    if document["expires_at"] <= now:
1016	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
1017	    if mode == "plain":
1018	        if allowlist[source] <= now:
1019	            raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
1020	    elif not _has_key_history(trust) and sources[source]["expires_at"] <= now:
1021	        # Legacy rule only: the pinned registry entry's own deadline applies.
1022	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)

1025	def _recompute_range_tail(anchor: dict, blocks_raw: list) -> list[Block]:
1026	    """Recompute and validate the delivered tail standalone from the anchor.
1027	
1028	    Mirrors the node's own range-tail rules: heights run consecutively from
1029	    ``anchor.height + 1``, the first ``prev_hash`` is the anchor hash and
1030	    later ones link internally, every transaction's tx_id and Ed25519
1031	    signature verifies, tx_ids are unique across the tail and ascending
1032	    inside each block, Merkle roots and block hashes recompute, and a pending
1033	    block may only sit at the tail tip. Every field is checked on the *raw*
1034	    JSON value; type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height,
1035	    non-positive or non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while
1036	    recomputation mismatches stay ``integrity``.
1037	    """
1038	    blocks: list[Block] = []
1039	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
1040	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(blocks_raw):
1041	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
1042	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1043	        height = block_raw.get("height")
1044	        prev_hash = block_raw.get("prev_hash")
1045	        merkle_root = block_raw.get("merkle_root")
1046	        block_hash = block_raw.get("block_hash")
1047	        status = block_raw.get("status")
1048	        txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
1049	        # Same rule as the whole-chain recomputation: a height of the wrong
1050	        # type or sign is a field-type defect (input), never coerced.
1051	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
1052	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1053	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
1054	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1055	        if not crypto.is_hex64(merkle_root) or not crypto.is_hex64(block_hash):
1056	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1057	        if status not in ("pending", "confirmed") or not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
1058	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1059	        if height != anchor["height"] + 1 + position:
1060	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1061	        expected_prev = (
1062	            anchor["block_hash"] if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
1063	        )
1064	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
1065	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1066	        if position < len(blocks_raw) - 1 and status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
1067	            # A pending block may only sit at the tail tip.
1068	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1069	
1070	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
1071	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
1072	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):
1073	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1074	            sender = raw_tx.get("from")
1075	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
1076	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
1077	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
1078	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")
1079	            if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
1080	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1081	            if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
1082	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1083	            # The raw amount must already be a non-boolean positive integer —
1084	            # never a coercible string, float or bool.
1085	            if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
1086	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1087	            if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
1088	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1089	            message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
1090	            tx_id = crypto.compute_tx_id(message)
1091	            if stored_tx_id != tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
1092	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1093	            if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
1094	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1095	            if tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
1096	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1097	            seen_tx_ids.add(tx_id)
1098	            tx_ids.append(tx_id)
1099	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
1100	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1101	        if crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids) != merkle_root:
1102	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1103	        recomputed = compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle_root)
1104	        if recomputed != block_hash:
1105	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1106	        # Parsed only after every raw field has checked out; never trusted for
